holidays.name: National Spider-Man Day
holidays.description: Fans of the web-slinging superhero swing into action by watching the movies, reading the comics, and wearing red and blue. Expect plenty of 'with great power comes great responsibility' quotes.
holidays.origin: Spider-Man debuted in Amazing Fantasy #15, cover-dated August 1962, created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko. Fans have marked August 1 as an unofficial celebration of the character.
holidays.funFact: Stan Lee reportedly got the idea after watching a fly crawl up a wall, and his publisher initially thought audiences would hate a spider hero because people fear spiders.

holidays.name: National Girlfriend Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate your girlfriend, or your close gal pals, with flowers, dinners, and sweet gestures. Friends and partners alike are encouraged to say thanks.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew through social media and greeting card culture, with no single documented founder. It is celebrated on August 1 in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Many people use the day for group celebrations among friends, so it is often about friendship as much as romance.

holidays.name: Yorkshire Day
holidays.description: Proud Yorkshire folk celebrate their county with flag-waving, Yorkshire pudding, and a ceremonial reading of the Declaration of Integrity at local events. It is a day of fierce regional pride.
holidays.origin: It was started in 1975 by the Yorkshire Ridings Society, a group that wanted to protest local government boundary changes. August 1 was chosen because it marks the anniversary of the abolition of slavery in the British Empire in 1834, which Yorkshire politician William Wilberforce helped bring about.
holidays.funFact: The Yorkshire Day proclamation is read in places such as town squares by a town crier, who also declares that Yorkshire is a great place.

holidays.name: National Raspberry Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: Celebrate with a slice of creamy, tangy, pink-tinted dessert. Whether homemade or from a bakery, this is a perfect excuse to indulge in summer berries and cream.
holidays.origin: This food observance is part of the American tradition of unofficial national food days, which are popularized by food bloggers, bakeries, and social media.
holidays.funFact: Raspberries are not technically single berries, but clusters of tiny fruits called drupelets, with each one holding a seed.

holidays.name: International Optimist Day
holidays.description: Bring on the sunny side up. This day encourages a positive outlook, and people try to see the glass half full, or at least refillable.
holidays.origin: This is an informal awareness day that encourages cheerful thinking, and it has been promoted by motivational groups and online communities.
holidays.funFact: Studies have linked optimism to better heart health and longer life, so smiling might literally be good for you.
